subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — isolation criteria & ops evidence requests
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Ortiz <elaine.ortiz@finlake.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — isolation criteria & ops evidence requests

Hi Elaine — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of FinLake requirements we noted on the call:
- Primary requirement: strong data isolation for PHI/pseudonymized financial datasets
- Preferred control plane: customer-managed VPC (Private) if we can show KMS/BYOK and audit log residency
- Alternative: Dedicated capacity with strict tenant fencing if Private is operationally prohibitive for the initial rollout

Open items / asks from FinLake for Redwood to address before procurement:
1) Evidence of control plane residency options (diagram + explanation of what data is stored in our control plane vs GPUs).
2) KMS/BYOK flow and whether customer keys can be used for model KV cache and logs.
3) Audit log retention and access model for Private vs Dedicated.
4) Network controls: peering options, egress rules, and any required firewall/IP allowlists.

Attachments: I’ve attached the call notes and a short checklist we’ll use to map features to your list (attached as "FinLake_Security_Requirements_20250510.pdf").

Proposed next steps: 
- I’ll pull together a short one-page mapping (Private vs Dedicated) that highlights differences for each of your items above.
- Marissa will coordinate a short technical walkthrough if you want to see the Private control plane UI and KMS options.
- If you can, please share any internal docs (network diagrams, minimal compliance checklist) so we can pre-populate our evidence pack.

Would you prefer a focused ops demo next week (30 min) or a deeper security review (45–60 min) with your Security team?

Thanks —
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

---
Attachment stub: FinLake_Security_Requirements_20250510.pdf (pdf, 212 KB)
From: Elaine Ortiz <elaine.ortiz@finlake.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: FinLake Security <security@finlake.com>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2025 17:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — isolation criteria & ops evidence requests

Thanks, Connor — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Control plane residency: we need to know exactly what metadata (request headers, tokens, any prompt/response metadata) would transit Redwood control plane for both Hosted and Private modes. If Private can fully avoid sending logs/metadata to Redwood-hosted control plane that strongly pushes us to Private.

2) BYOK/KMS: does Redwood allow customer KMS for encrypting model artifacts and token caches, or only for data-at-rest in object storage? We want to understand the scope.

3) Auditability: our auditors want a ready-to-present doc that lists log types (access logs, admin actions, service-to-service calls) and retention windows for Private vs Dedicated. 

4) Network Peering: we will need a prescriptive list of ports and CIDR ranges to lock down.

We can do a short ops demo next Wednesday (May 14) at 10:00am PT. I’ll invite our Security lead (Jamal Rahman) if that works. We'll also attach our internal minimal compliance checklist to the ticket for you to ingest.

–Elaine
Director, Product Security | FinLake
elaine.ortiz@finlake.com

---
Attachment stub: FinLake_minimal_compliance_checklist.xlsx (xls, 56 KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Ortiz <elaine.ortiz@finlake.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2025 18:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — isolation criteria & ops evidence requests

Hi Elaine — great to meet you on the call, and thanks for the clear asks. I’m Marissa (Solutions Engineering) — I’ll run the technical walkthrough and consolidate the evidence pack for your auditors. Quick notes on the items you raised, and what we’ll deliver ahead of the demo: 

Control plane residency (what we will deliver)
- One-page diagram that separates Customer VPC / Private control plane (what stays in your network) vs Redwood-managed control plane.
- Explicit list of metadata types and whether they are sent off-host in each deployment mode. (We’ll flag anything that must be proxied through Redwood.)

KMS/BYOK
- For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for control-plane secrets and object storage keys; we will document current limitations (e.g., certain ephemeral caches on GPU nodes require key-wrapping by Redwood-managed HSM unless configured for on-prem only).

Audit logs & retention
- We’ll provide a table of log types (admin, API access, model invocation) and default retention for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. For Private we can configure retention to meet your policy (we’ll note the operational tradeoffs).

Network peering & ports
- I’ll attach an architecture diagram and a prescriptive ports/CIDR spreadsheet. For Private we support VPC peering, private endpoints, and forced egress through customer NAT. For Dedicated we provide IP allowlists and dedicated subnets.

Operational requests from us (what will speed the process)
- Your minimal compliance checklist (thanks for sharing)
- A network diagram showing where you intend to place the control plane endpoints and any egress/NAT devices
- Preferred demo audience (ops vs security) so we tailor the walkthrough

I’ll drop the one-pager + diagram in the HubSpot deal folder and share a Drive link before the demo. Connor — can you lock the May 14 10:00am PT time and send a calendar invite with a short agenda (30–40 min: 20 min demo + 10–20 min Q&A)? Vivek — can you be on the call to address BYOK/KMS specifics?

Thanks — looking forward to the walkthrough.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (206) 555-0123

Date: Sun, 11 May 2025 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — isolation criteria & ops evidence requests

Thanks Marissa — that plan looks good. I invited Jamal (our Security lead) and he confirmed May 14 at 10:00am PT works for a technical ops + security walkthrough. Please include the one-pager and the ports/CIDR sheet ahead of the session so we can circulate internally. 

Pre-demo preference: given our compliance timeline and existing on-prem tooling, we are favoring a Private VPC deployment if Redwood can demonstrate BYOK for control-plane keys and no metadata exfiltration to Redwood-managed infrastructure. If any of those are hard blockers, we’ll consider Dedicated as a fallback but need the tradeoffs spelled out.

We’ll upload our network diagram and the minimal checklist to the HubSpot deal folder by Monday EOD. Looking forward to the demo.

Best,
Elaine
Director, Product Security | FinLake
elaine.ortiz@finlake.com
